records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list the Hancock peaking plant. EIA's monthly generator file for September 2026 lists EIA plant 1730, Hancock, owned by DTE Electric Company, in Oakland County. Its Operating sheet rows read: "Hancock | 5 | 41.8 | Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine | 1970" and "Hancock | 6 | 41.8 | Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine | 1966". Generators 1 and 3 are 19 MW each. The point given is latitude 42.5497 and longitude -83.4425. The state air permit staff report at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/3438450417378425065 says the site at 1781 Haggerty Highway in Commerce Township has two Westinghouse combustion turbine generators of 18.5 MW each and two jet turbine generators of 41.27 MW each. The two jet units are Pratt and Whitney FT4 twin pack sets, which are aeroderivative turbines. The report also says one 18.5 MW unit and one 21.5 MW unit were retired on December 22, 2019. The two jet units together make an aeroderivative set of 83.6 MW, which is above the 50 MW threshold, so the plant is an add. The two 19 MW Westinghouse frame units are each under 50 MW and are left out. The staff report says the units were installed between April 1966 and May 1970.

records.researcher_notes: MISO's generator interconnection queue, read through the data behind its interactive queue page at https://www.misoenergy.org/planning/resource-utilization/GI_Queue/gi-interactive-queue/, lists request J3922 in Branch County, Michigan. It is a gas combined cycle project of 1,445 MW connecting at the Hiple substation on the METC transmission system. It was queued on March 4, 2025, is in the 2025 study cycle, phase 1, with status "Pending Revision Approval", and asks for an in-service date of March 1, 2030. The same row is copied at https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/miso-j3922. No developer, plant name, utility filing or air permit names the project. It is not one of the Consumers Energy or DTE Electric gas plants in their 2026 resource plans, which are in Bay, Genesee, Monroe and Livingston counties. The plant is named after its substation and county because the request has no other name. A queue entry is enough to add a plant at announced. Not found: the owner, the turbine model, the exact site and the coordinates.

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this proposed plant. The state air permit to install 210-18 at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/1162895226898629589 was issued on August 21, 2019 to Thomas Township Energy, LLC for a site east of North Orr Road and north of Geddes Road in Hemlock, Saginaw County. It covers two natural gas combined cycle blocks, each one combustion turbine with a heat recovery boiler and one steam turbine, and each rated at a combined nominal 625 MW. That is 1,250 MW in all. The turbine maker is listed as to be determined. The state permit portal lists the permit as terminated on September 7, 2021, and the site has no other permit or document there. No news story, queue entry or utility filing names the project. GEM tracks cancelled projects from 2020 on, so it is added as cancelled in 2021. The status rests on one source, the state permit record, so it stays at medium confidence. The owner is a project company. The GEM entity system has no entry for Thomas Township Energy LLC, so it would be a new entity.
records.action: Create the plant in Hemlock, Saginaw County, Michigan, then add the two units below as cancelled, cancellation year 2021, with no start year. Add Thomas Township Energy LLC as a new owner entity.
